projects.documentation:
# Meeting Note Action Extractor

Upload multiple meeting note text files → batch extract action items → output as spreadsheet-ready rows.

Each action item includes:
- Task description
- Owner (person responsible)
- Optional due date if mentioned

The output list is directly exportable to CSV/XLSX from the UI.

# Homework Grader

1. Upload rubric (single text file)
2. Upload student homeworks (many text files)
3. Pipeline parses both
4. Grades each homework against rubric
5. Outputs spreadsheet with one row per student-question

Export results as CSV/XLSX from the viewer.

modules.note: Pipeline input document

models.name: RubricQuestion
models.description: One question in the marking schema.

models.description: One section in the derived marking schema.

models.description: Structured rubric — assignment sections and questions to grade against.

[subs] : []; const text = (s) => (typeof s?.content === "string" ? s.content : typeof s?.body === "string" ? s.body : ""); const name = (s, i) => (typeof s?.filename === "string" && s.filename ? s.filename : typeof s?.doc_id === "string" ? s.doc_id : `student_${i + 1}.md`); return { marking_schema: { filename: "marking_schema.json", content: stableJson(schema ?? {}) }, student_submissions: list.map((s, i) => ({ filename: name(s, i), content: text(s) })) }; }

modules.label: Flatten Sections
modules.note: One gradable row per student × rubric question.
modules.inputDescription: GraderWork — marking_schema Document plus list of student submission Documents

[]; } catch {} } const out = []; for (const sub of work.student_submissions ?? []) { const content = sub.content ?? ""; const student = (content.match(/Student:\s*([^\n]+)/i) || [])[1]?.trim() || sub.filename?.replace(/\.md$/i, "") || "student"; for (const sec of sections) { for (const q of sec.questions ?? []) { const qRe = new RegExp(`\\*\\*${q.question_id}\\.\\*\\*[\\s\\S]*?(Student work:[^\\n]*)`, "i"); const workLine = (content.match(qRe) || [])[1]?.trim() ?? ""; out.push({ student_label: student, section_id: sec.section_id, title: `${sec.title} — ${q.question_id}`, body: `${q.prompt ?? ""}${workLine ? "\n" + workLine : ""}`, max_score: q.max_score ?? 1, criteria: q.marking_criteria ?? sec.criteria ?? "" }); } } } return out; }

modules.label: Grade Each Section
modules.note: List of GradableSection objects — student_label, question body, max_score, and criteria
modules.inputDescription: List of GradableSection objects — student_label, question body, max_score, and criteria
modules.prompt: Apply criteria literally and deterministically. When criteria lists alternate bands (e.g. 'award exactly N pts if…'), check those bands before summing components — pick exactly one band score, never mix. Score MUST equal the exact points from the matching band or component sum — use only point values explicitly named in criteria (no rounding, no extra credit, no in-between scores). Score is an integer from 0 to max_score inclusive. Copy max_score from input unchanged. Set correct=true iff score equals max_score; never set correct=true when score is below max_score. Copy student_label and section_id exactly from input. When correct is false, mistake_explanation must cite the rubric clause applied and state the student's wrong value vs the required value. When correct is true, mistake_explanation must be an empty string.

modules.label: Final Output
modules.inputDescription: List of SectionGrade rows — student_label, section_id, score, max_score, correct, mistake_explanation (one row per student × rubric question)

modules.label: Grade Count Check
modules.note: len(Student Submissions) × len(Marking Questions List) = len(Final Output)
modules.inputDescription: List of SectionGrade rows — student_label, section_id, score, max_score, correct, mistake_explanation (one row per student × rubric question)

fallbackList.python:
n_students = len_of(step('Student Submissions'))
n_questions = len_of(step('Marking Questions List'))
n_out = len_of(step('Final Output'))
if n_students * n_questions != n_out:
    raise ValueError(f'expected {n_students}×{n_questions}={n_students * n_questions} grades, got {n_out}')

# MATH 301 Real Analysis — Problem Set 4 — Student: Priya Nair

## Section A — Integration and limits (20 pts)

**Q1.** Evaluate \(\int_0^1 3x^2 e^{x^3}\,dx\). Show the substitution explicitly.  
Student work: Let \(u = x^3\), so \(du = 3x^2\,dx\); the bounds transform as \(u : 0 \to 1\), giving \(\int_0^1 e^u\,du = e - 1\).

**Q2.** Compute \(\lim_{n \to \infty} \left(1 + \frac{2}{n}\right)^{n}\).  
Student work: Write \(\left(1 + \frac{2}{n}\right)^{n} = e^{n \ln(1 + 2/n)}\); since \(n \ln(1 + 2/n) \to 2\), the limit is \(e^2\).

## Section B — Series convergence (20 pts)

**Q3.** Determine whether \(\sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \frac{n!}{n^n}\) converges. Justify with a named test.  
Student work: Ratio test — \(\frac{a_{n+1}}{a_n} = \left(\frac{n}{n+1}\right)^{n} \to \frac{1}{e} < 1\), hence the series converges.

**Q4.** Prove that \(\sum_{n=2}^{\infty} \frac{1}{n \ln^2 n}\) converges.  
Student work: The terms are smaller than \(\frac{1}{n^2}\), so it converges by comparison with \(\sum \frac{1}{n^2}\).

pendingCreates.documentation:
# Meeting Note Action Extractor

Upload multiple meeting note text files → batch extract action items → output as spreadsheet-ready rows.

Each action item includes:
- Task description
- Owner (person responsible)
- Optional due date if mentioned

The output list is directly exportable to CSV/XLSX from the UI.

# Homework Grader

1. Upload rubric (single text file)
2. Upload student homeworks (many text files)
3. Pipeline parses both
4. Grades each homework against rubric
5. Outputs spreadsheet with one row per student-question

Export results as CSV/XLSX from the viewer.

[subs] : []; const text = (s) => (typeof s?.content === "string" ? s.content : typeof s?.body === "string" ? s.body : ""); const name = (s, i) => (typeof s?.filename === "string" && s.filename ? s.filename : typeof s?.doc_id === "string" ? s.doc_id : `student_${i + 1}.md`); return { marking_schema: { filename: "marking_schema.json", content: stableJson(schema ?? {}) }, student_submissions: list.map((s, i) => ({ filename: name(s, i), content: text(s) })) }; }

fallbackList.typescript: (work) => { let sections = []; const ms = work.marking_schema; if (ms?.sections) sections = ms.sections; else if (typeof ms?.content === "string") { try { sections = JSON.parse(ms.content).sections ?? []; } catch {} } const out = []; for (const sub of work.student_submissions ?? []) { const content = sub.content ?? ""; const student = (content.match(/Student:\s*([^\n]+)/i) || [])[1]?.trim() || sub.filename?.replace(/\.md$/i, "") || "student"; for (const sec of sections) { for (const q of sec.questions ?? []) { const qRe = new RegExp(`\\*\\*${q.question_id}\\.\\*\\*[\\s\\S]*?(Student work:[^\\n]*)`, "i"); const workLine = (content.match(qRe) || [])[1]?.trim() ?? ""; out.push({ student_label: student, section_id: sec.section_id, title: `${sec.title} — ${q.question_id}`, body: `${q.prompt ?? ""}${workLine ? "\n" + workLine : ""}`, max_score: q.max_score ?? 1, criteria: q.marking_criteria ?? sec.criteria ?? "" }); } } } return out; }

modules.prompt: Apply criteria literally and deterministically. When criteria lists alternate bands (e.g. 'award exactly N pts if…'), check those bands before summing components — pick exactly one band score, never mix. Score MUST equal the exact points from the matching band or component sum — use only point values explicitly named in criteria (no rounding, no extra credit, no in-between scores). Score is an integer from 0 to max_score inclusive. Copy max_score from input unchanged. Set correct=true iff score equals max_score; never set correct=true when score is below max_score. Copy student_label and section_id exactly from input. When correct is false, mistake_explanation must cite the rubric clause applied and state the student's wrong value vs the required value. When correct is true, mistake_explanation must be an empty string.

modules.label: Final Output
modules.inputDescription: List of SectionGrade rows — student_label, section_id, score, max_score, correct, mistake_explanation (one row per student × rubric question)

modules.inputDescription: List of SectionGrade rows — student_label, section_id, score, max_score, correct, mistake_explanation (one row per student × rubric question)
